(1) Optimizer. Muon with decoupled weight decay and the update RMS matched to AdamW's (Moonshot, "Muon is Scalable"): momentum 0.95 with Nesterov, 5 Newton-Schulz steps (coefficients 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) in float32 (V100 has no bf16), update = 0.2*sqrt(max(fan_out, fan_in)) * orthogonalised momentum, W <- W - lr*(update + wd*W). It acts on exactly the backbone's hidden matrices, the parameters muP already marks matrix-like (infshape.ninf()==2: per block qkv, attention out, the two MLP layers; 32 matrices, most of the weights). Everything else stays on AdamW exactly as in the baseline (no weight decay, the L2 term in the loss): linear_in and linear_out (muP's input and readout), biases, norms, the particle embedding, the sign head, the framesnet and the diagram encoder (both standard parametrisation, outside muP). Implementation: our own ~80-line optim/muon.py, one torch.optim.Optimizer holding both kinds of group (so CosineAnnealingLR, clipping, EMA, fused AdamW and the fine-tune lr groups work unchanged), a new optimizer: MuonAdamW branch in base_experiment._init_optimizer, a CPU unit test (orthogonality, RMS 0.2, muP scale). Not a pip package: torch.optim.Muon needs torch >= 2.9, Keller Jordan's muon package is built around torch.distributed; ours needs only matmul, so torch 2.1.2 is fine (CC venv not checked for any package).
(2) muP. MuAdamW divides a hidden matrix's lr by its width multiplier (fan_in/base fan_in = 4 at 8 heads, base 2): Adam's update is close to low rank, its spectral norm grows like the width, and 1/width keeps it O(1). Muon's orthogonalised update has every singular value 1; with the Moonshot factor its spectral norm grows like sqrt(width), so the muP rule for Muon matrices is lr/sqrt(width multiplier), not 1/width (the spectral condition, Yang-Simon-Bernstein). Implemented as the factor 0.2*sqrt(max(fan_out,fan_in))/sqrt(width multiplier) = the Moonshot RMS match at the base width, and the lr is then width-independent. At 8 heads the Muon update RMS is therefore 2x MuAdamW's at the same lr number (0.1*lr against ~0.05*lr). This test runs at one width only, so muP transfer across width is not tested.
(3) Baseline, not rerun: the catalog_v3 short pretraining with the adopted dimensionless target (run FA-ccin2p3-ff0533da, runs/catalog_v3_short/dimensionless): hp58's config, 4264 steps (5 epochs of 1e4 events x 1397 pools), batch 16384, lr 8.94e-3, L2 4.96e-7, warmup 0.158, eta_min 1.8e-10, EMA 0.941, MSE with the arithmetic mean, sign head, diagram encoder; one seed; trained in 61.5 min (0.86 s/step), job 1.65 h with its reads.
